Based solely on the quick ratio, which company is most liquid?

The quick ratio is calculated as (Cash + Marketable securities + Receivables) / Current liabilities, using the common-size percentages given. Company X: (15.6% + 3.4% + 10.9%) / 28.6% = 29.9% / 28.6% = 1.045. Company Y: (12.0% + 5.1% + 12.7%) / 28.2% = 29.8% / 28.2% = 1.057. Company Z: (2.0% + 12.0% + 4.8%) / 17.1% = 18.8% / 17.1% = 1.099. Company Z has the highest quick ratio, making it the most liquid of the three companies based solely on this measure.
